segments.text: Why are the school buses in every movie and TV show always yellow? It's not a coincidence. It's a decision.
Early school buses were often just farm wagons with benches, and America had no national standard for how they should look.
Then, in April {1939,|nineteen thirty-nine,} a professor named Frank Cyr gathered officials from all forty-eight states, bus builders, and paint experts at Columbia University for a week.
They agreed on forty-four national standards. One of them was the color: a yellow-orange called National School Bus Chrome.
The reason given? Black lettering stands out best on yellow, even in the half-dark of dawn and dusk. Right when children are waiting at the roadside.
Today that color has an official name, National School Bus Glossy Yellow, and a federal color number: {13432.|one three four three two.}
So the yellow bus in your favorite movie isn't a director's choice. It's the legacy of one week-long meeting in {1939.|nineteen thirty-nine.} If you enjoyed this, like and follow for more.
